The Good Studio briefing

Make good happen

You are joining a creative studio with a purpose. Your job is to invent a charity and build a connected digital campaign that persuades people to care and act.

Your complete campaign

The big picture

Across five short workbooks, you will move from an idea to a polished charity campaign. Each product should feel connected through the same audience, message and visual identity.

Campaign brief quality

What good looks like
  • A clearly defined charity cause and mission.
  • A specific target audience with real needs.
  • A campaign objective that explains the intended impact.
  • A suitable platform chosen for its features.
  • Measurable success criteria for later evaluation.

The campaign formula

Remember this

Strong campaigns are planned. They connect a clear purpose to a specific target audience, then use the right platform, message and digital asset to encourage action.

Learn and apply

What is digital marketing?

Digital marketing uses connected technologies to promote an organisation, cause, product or service. It is broader than social media alone.

Digital marketing uses websites, apps, email, search engines, social platforms and digital media to reach and influence an audience.

Know the difference

Platform: where the content appears.

Digital asset: the content people see or use.

Campaign: connected activities working towards one objective.

Task: digital, traditional or both?

Required

Classify every example. Some campaigns deliberately connect online and offline methods.

An influencer shares a charity video with a donation link.
A leaflet is delivered through local residents' doors.
A sponsored result appears when someone searches for animal rescue.
A charity appeal is broadcast on local radio.
A printed poster includes a QR code linking to a campaign website.
A fundraising event is advertised through social posts and newspaper adverts.
Reach the right people

Your feed is not random

Digital platforms use information about people and their behaviour to decide which content is most relevant. Marketers use this targeting to reach particular groups.

Meet Maya

Maya regularly watches dog-rescue videos, searches for local volunteering and lives near Bridgend. Her feed shows a video from a local animal charity.

Why might Maya have seen it?

Target audiences

Required

A target audience can be described using characteristics such as age, location and interests. These details should affect the platform, message and content format.

Age
Location
Interests
Needs
Responsible marketing

Targeting can be useful, but organisations must handle personal data responsibly and avoid misleading or exploiting an audience.

Task: choose by feature, not fashion

Required

Match each campaign to the platform type that best suits its audience and content.

Young people's wellbeingA 20-second emotional video aimed at teenagers, designed to be shared quickly.
Local winter supportUpdates about nearby warm spaces and volunteering, mainly aimed at adults in the local community.
Understanding ocean pollutionA detailed five-minute story using interviews, facts and footage to explain the issue.
Plan before you publish

Six connected decisions

A campaign is coherent when every decision works towards the same objective. Build the planning sequence, then examine digital marketing's power and responsibility.

Build the campaign sequence

Required

Select the planning decisions in the most logical order. Start with why the campaign exists and finish with what people should do.

Campaign vocabulary

Mission: why the charity exists.

Campaign objective: what this campaign should achieve.

Call to action: what the audience should do next.

Success criteria: measurable signs that show whether it worked.

Task: power and responsibility

Required

Decide whether each statement is an opportunity created by digital marketing or a risk that needs managing.

A small charity can reach thousands of relevant people at relatively low cost.
Views, clicks and donations can help measure whether a campaign is working.
An organisation could misuse personal information when targeting adverts.
Misleading claims could spread quickly and damage trust in the charity.

Digital marketing key terms

Digital marketingUsing digital technologies and channels to promote an organisation, cause, product or service.
PlatformAn online service where content is created, shared or viewed.
Digital assetA piece of campaign content, such as a logo, image, advert, webpage or video.
CampaignConnected marketing activities designed to achieve one main objective.
Target audienceThe specific group of people a campaign is designed to reach.
TargetingUsing audience characteristics and behaviour to show relevant content to particular people.
EngagementHow people interact with content, including views, likes, shares, comments and clicks.
Call to actionA clear instruction telling the audience what to do next.
MissionThe reason a charity exists and the long-term change it wants to create.
Campaign objectiveThe specific result a particular campaign should achieve.
Success criteriaSpecific statements used to judge whether a product or campaign has succeeded.
CoherentConsistent and logically connected, with every part working towards the same purpose.
